page: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, featuring AMD EPYC 9R14 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz. The system provides 64 dedicated physical cores mapping directly to 64 vCPUs with a single thread per core, removing hyperthreading contention. It is configured with 256.0 GB of high-frequency 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, complemented by advanced x86_64 instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI. The platform provides a 25 Gbps baseline network interface, while local NVMe storage is omitted, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk access.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier multi-core computing capability and high memory throughput. The server records a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,761.0 and a stress-ng multi-core throughput of 196,723.64, both residing in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 268.22 GB/sec read and 151.76 GB/sec write throughput. High parallelism translates directly into real-world application throughput: the instance manages 122.99 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 68,760.0 in Geekbench Clang software compilation. In machine learning benchmarks, it achieves 5,127.7 tokens per second prompt processing on 135M parameter models and maintains 45.47 tokens per second generation speed on 7B parameter architectures.

From an efficiency standpoint, the 1:1 physical core allocation provides predictable CPU execution without thread-sharing degradation, making the resource density cost-effective for heavily threaded applications. The absence of integrated local storage shifts storage IOPS entirely to network storage volumes, which represents a deliberate architectural tradeoff. The balanced compute and DDR5 memory profile makes the instance well suited for large in-memory caches, distributed databases, large-scale CI/CD build environments, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 64 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs operating at 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading overhead. The system incorporates 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory across a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, alongside 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and no local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier multi-threaded throughput, scoring 21,761 in Geekbench multi-core and processing 122.99 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware vector extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 bolster performance in numeric computing and CPU-based machine learning inference. While the absence of bundled local NVMe storage necessitates external EBS volumes, its high raw core density and fast memory bandwidth offer efficient processing capacity for enterprise databases, distributed caching, CI/CD compilation, and mid-tier LLM inference.
